title: MZ MZifier - Convert plugins from RPG Maker MV to RPG Maker MZ

posts.author: DrFreeman
posts.body:
Introducing the MZifier, a tool to convert plugins from MV to MZ. You can download it from
GitHub repository
or the
direct zip file here
.
Instructions:
Download the zip file
Move your script to the same folder as the executable with Python312.dll
Open Command Prompt or Terminal to your saved folder
Use mzifier.exe script_name.js
The new script will be converted to script_name_MZ.js in the same folder
Below is an image of converting a simple plugin.
The software is currently in alpha. It does not modify the original script, but I always recommend making a backup. I have converted several plugins. The software license is CC 4.0 with attribution. Please attribute the company Paradise Union. Please provide credit as a special thanks. There is no cost. It can be used in commercial or non-commercial projects
Depending on the script you are converting, you should get permission from the original copyright holder unless they have given you permission to alter their work for your project. The copyright holders of the plugins usually provide support. Any alterations could be outside of their support.
Roadmap items:
Support for a standardized RPG Maker template
Add a GUI
Linux/Mac support
Any script to script version of RPG Maker
If you run into any issues with the software, please leave a message on my
GitHub under issues
. Please leave a comment for any criticisms or suggestions.

posts.author: Aerosys
posts.body:
I'm a bit conflicted. The ability to run MV plugins in MZ is something the community has wished for since the beginning. When we had FOSSIL, it ended up in a lot of drama. The creator promised the Holy Grail, but we haven't got it, and the rest is a story for another day.
Long story short: Of course, we all want such a plugin or tool, but it can lead to a lot of disappointment when it does not fulfill the promises.
Looking at your code, I can already see that it only converts the tip of the iceberg. I doubt that it can convert even 5% of all MV plugins. Well, to be fair, it's in alpha. It probably can convert more plugins the more work you invest. And there's a lot of work to do.

I would be curious to test all MV plugins, but I don't have the time to make an automated tool for it. I made this for my project and thought I would share. I didn't run into any issues, so I thought I would release it. MZifier was made in Python. I chose Python because Microsoft had abandoned JScript and the WinUI template. C++ or a JS executable were alternative options, but turning Python scripts into executables is easier for me than JS. The Python syntax is (often) easier on audiences than C++.
Side note: I have thought about an application that has an aggregated list of all plugins that users could download into their folders. It is way off to the side for me, but if someone wanted to build it, they can have my notes to make it. The best I had found was GitHub, Google, and also Sigmasuccour's Google Doc list. I had imagined something like a mix of the Linux canonical upgrade and the Google Play Store. People see a table of plugin's, click on which one they want, and goes to the project. Includes license information, tutorials, etc.
I digress, during the transition from VX Ace to MV, I saw many plugins that should be moved over. When I compared my tool to
https://www.ruby2js.com/
it seemed to compare in many regards. My code had fault protections if it is unable to understand. It will throw it over there. Other tools I tried didn't have that either. I try to find the opportunity in the situation when I know a script could break the tool. Prior to release, I didn't get approval for conversions, so I never tried. When I run into a plugin that doesn't convert, I'll update the converter.
I had only heard of FOSSIL less than two weeks ago, but I never had a chance to look at it. I find it interesting that he made it as a plugin for plugins. If I had seen FOSSIL, I would have substantially changed or even abandoned this little utility. After briefly looking through the plugin, his script is more technically designed for specific plugins. It is a good plugin. I might update my script to reflect the exceptions he included. JS to Python conversions can take time.
Regardless, it seems there is room for both of our solutions. Despite getting my MCSD and using MV the most, I never got into plugin development with MV. I have become more familiar with the MZ style of making plugins. Converting plugins over works well for me.
If you find an error with the tool, please leave it in the GitHub issues. If you run into an error with converting and it's approved by the copyright holder, I would be curious what doesn't get converted over. I am uncertain how much this tool can convert all scripts, but if someone finds something, I would be willing to add it in. I'm working on a large project, so maybe I might run into the same conversion issue.

I feel like I have to reply to this, but honestly, the discussion really comes down to personal philosophy. I was there when this happened, and it’s sorta relevant to this thread, so I see no reason not to share.
The issue being talked about is the negatives of something like FOSSIL in the new MZ ecosystem — where bugs and unstable systems start becoming the norm because they’re not exactly built for MZ’s new backend. There’s a legitimate fear here because of the XP days, when SDKs tied you down to a framework and forced you to only work with specific plugins.
What that staff personally thinks should not affect you as a plugin developer.
We had our share of conflict with the same staff back in the VX/Ace era too, especially about how to handle public plugins. Like, is it really good to have five different Yanfly Engines for a single engine? Yanfly believed he was pushing RM to do things it wasn’t meant to do, which hurt performance and led to nerfs. Meanwhile, parts of the fanbase disagreed and would get mad about YER, YEZ, YEM, Yanfly Engine, etc. It’s basically the same situation all over again.
RPG Maker has a lot of history and baggage when it comes to plugin philosophy. Paid plugins have nothing to do with it. They’ve been around since the XP days.

I'm unfamiliar with the dramatic events related to Fossil or Retro.js, but I have little interest in knowing. Whether as a hobbyist or a professional, RPG Maker, to me, is about delivering quality experiences that children and adults can enjoy. Hopefully, MZifier can help people retain old plugins and projects.
Back in RPG Maker (RPGM) 2k3 and VX Ace, we wished there were tools we could easily convert plugins. Backwards compatibility was a best practice for the time. We had to abandon several things to keep up. I had no other reason to learn Ruby than RPGM. Before purchasing RPGM MZ, I had read several stories of people unable to convert projects or plugins. Later, the company provided an update to convert over projects. I was quite proud that the company had adapted; the developers did a good job. Converting legacy code or projects is difficult. A significant number of RPGM users had dedicated a significant amount of effort, money, and time to many plugins and projects. I think MZifier can help the company and others minimize the depreciation of their dedication. There are still many good people in the RPG Maker community and I believe we can all make it even better.

It is no problem.
Let's extract the zip folder to it's own folder. It could be something like c:/users/user_name/downloads/MZifier.
We'll move the desired Javascript file to the MZifier folder. In my sample I used basic_plugin.js.
We'll open Command Crompt or terminal. Click on the start menu (or hold windows + r) and type Command Prompt. It will open a black window with the starting directory as
either c:/windows/system32> or c:/users/user_name>.
We're going to need to change the directory to the MZifier folder.
You'll want to change the directory with CD "c:/users/user_name/downloads/MZifier". You will use the directory of where you extracted MZifier.
After that, you just type mzifier script_name.js.
This is a picture of me doing it in my Command Prompt.
At the end, it will create another script with the _MZ.js as the new script. If it ran into any issues or errors, it has a report. For my file it was basic_plugin_MZ.js.report.txt.

Before taking a side project more seriously, it is critical to identify any potential obstacles like that. Thank you! I was thinking about a similar design to requesting Linux update repositories or Visual Studio Code extensions. Friendly, yet professional. My initial plan was to post a link to their source. The source code and executables would remain in their control. I would respect the developers' wishes to avoid being available, but I would find it a little odd that a developer wouldn't want free press for their plugin for easy access or purchases. A good example might be older plugins like the transition from Yanfly to VisuStella plugins.
I know many of the old Brazillian and Japanese developers miss the old camaraderie we used to have for developing RPG Maker games. It would be nice to provide an open invitation to those who were never included in international game development teams or projects. Many of the countries' laws can be very different, but I believe there is a way we can accommodate licensing. It could be something easy that developers could agree on like Apache, Creative Commons, or MIT licensing.
The last major concern is that translating plugins and software has always been an issue. It had existed long before RPG Maker. Simple, poorly translated tags or titles can lead to seriously undesirable results. But a developer or team with ingenuity might be able to overcome these difficulties and forge a great path for others. We had done it before and we can do it again.
If you can think of any possible problems, just throw it out there.
We just prioritize them and work through them.
